input.brief: This session works on the refund path of the orchard-api service. The work is to get refunds on POST /v2/refunds idempotent in time for orchard-api 0.19.0. In progress: internal/refund/dedupe.go is being rewritten so that its lookup reads the idem_keys table. It was decided to store idempotency keys for 72 hours. That window was chosen as the bank replays for up to 48 hours, plus one day of margin. Deduplication relies on a unique index over (merchant_id, idem_key), not on an advisory lock. Advisory locks had been getting lost under pgbouncer in transaction mode. Replaying a refund gives back the original 201 body and never a 409. The cause is that two merchant SDKs take a 409 as fatal and give up retrying. Amounts for refunds live in the amount_minor column as whole minor units. Floats had rounded a cent away on 3 of 10,000 test refunds. Calls to the ledger give up at 2 seconds and are retried twice. This follows from a ledger p99 of 1.1 seconds and from a third retry having doubled the queue depth. A partial refund on a charge older than 180 days is refused. The card scheme turns those down anyway and its error used to arrive two days late. refund.settled goes out only once the ledger has confirmed. Merchants had shipped goods back on an early webhook that then got reversed. Everything sits behind the refunds_v2_idem flag, which defaults to off. The operator asked for one merchant to run it for a week ahead of the rest. A ledger call slower than 800 ms still makes the refund handler answer 500. The staging database is still without migration 0042_idem_keys.sql. TestRefundReplay is flaky, about 1 run in 6, each time on a duplicate ledger entry. Waiting on the operator: do partial refunds over 250 EUR require a second approval? ORCHARD_HOOK_KEY_V1, a retired secret, is still what the webhook signer reads. Since the join went in, GET /v2/disputes/{id} has a p99 of 310 ms, up from 40 ms. Three endpoints in api/openapi.yaml are missing the Idempotency-Key header. Refunds in CHF are turned down by the sandbox bank at gateway.bank.test. 1,240 refunds sit in the retry queue, stuck in pending_ledger. An empty batch makes cmd/reconcile panic on a nil Settlement. Migrations must never be run against production from this session. Commit messages begin with the ticket id, for example ORCH-412. make lint-go has to pass ahead of each push. Files generated under gen/proto/ are not to be edited by hand. Replies to the operator stay in plain English and within 120 words. Later: the export job wants an index on refunds(created_at). The runbook page docs/runbooks/refund-replay.md remains to be written. Once 0.20.0 is out, the deprecated POST /v1/refund can be removed.

input.brief: This session works on the power budget of the marrow sensor firmware. Purpose: between LoRa transmissions the marrow sensor board should draw under 12 µA asleep. Being measured now: current on the VDD_RF rail while the radio is in standby. Timekeeping uses the LSE crystal for the RTC instead of the LSI oscillator. At minus 10 degrees the LSI was off by 4 seconds per hour. Before sleeping, PB3 to PB7 are switched to analog mode. Left floating, those inputs leaked roughly 20 µA. Layout: bootloader at 0x08000000, application at 0x08008000. Only addresses above the first 32 KiB are flashed by the field update tool. Sleep current is 84 µA, the accelerometer being left in normal mode. Coming out of STOP2 costs 31 ms, enough to miss the first RX window. The operator has yet to pick the reporting interval: 15-minute or 60-minute. Read the serial from OTP before flashing any board, always. A power figure is the mean over 5 runs lasting 60 seconds each. Register 0x2C, the regulator's low-power mode, is worth a try. Each build should log sleep current into tools/bench/sleep_log.csv.

input.brief: This session works on the refund path of the orchard-api service. The work is to get refunds on POST /v2/refunds idempotent in time for orchard-api 0.19.0. In progress: internal/refund/dedupe.go is being rewritten so that its lookup reads the idem_keys table. It was decided to store idempotency keys for 72 hours. That window was chosen as the bank replays for up to 48 hours, plus one day of margin. Deduplication relies on a unique index over (merchant_id, idem_key), not on an advisory lock. Advisory locks had been getting lost under pgbouncer in transaction mode. Replaying a refund gives back the original 201 body and never a 409. The cause is that two merchant SDKs take a 409 as fatal and give up retrying. Amounts for refunds live in the amount_minor column as whole minor units. Floats had rounded a cent away on 3 of 10,000 test refunds. Calls to the ledger give up at 2 seconds and are retried twice. This follows from a ledger p99 of 1.1 seconds and from a third retry having doubled the queue depth. A partial refund on a charge older than 180 days is refused. The card scheme turns those down anyway and its error used to arrive two days late. refund.settled goes out only once the ledger has confirmed. Merchants had shipped goods back on an early webhook that then got reversed. Everything sits behind the refunds_v2_idem flag, which defaults to off. The operator asked for one merchant to run it for a week ahead of the rest. A ledger call slower than 800 ms still makes the refund handler answer 500. The staging database is still without migration 0042_idem_keys.sql. TestRefundReplay is flaky, about 1 run in 6, each time on a duplicate ledger entry. Waiting on the operator: do partial refunds over 250 EUR require a second approval? ORCHARD_HOOK_KEY_V1, a retired secret, is still what the webhook signer reads. Since the join went in, GET /v2/disputes/{id} has a p99 of 310 ms, up from 40 ms. Three endpoints in api/openapi.yaml are missing the Idempotency-Key header. input.brief: This session works on the upload path of the kestrel-sync daemon. The objective is for kestrel-sync to resume interrupted uploads, not start again at byte 0. Under way: a chunk journal, in crates/transfer/src/journal.rs. The journal is append-only and gets fsynced every 16 chunks. Syncing after each chunk had cost 38 % of throughput. BLAKE3 replaces SHA-256 for chunk hashes. On the ARM boxes hashing took 22 % of CPU time. Any resume older than 7 days is abandoned and the upload starts over. The server garbage-collects partial uploads after one week. If the server has lost the last 2 chunks, resuming dies with E_CHUNK_GAP. On macOS runners the resume_after_kill integration test hangs once 90 seconds have passed. Still to be confirmed by the operator: are 8 MiB chunks fine on metered links? crates/transfer must not use unwrap(); errors are returned as TransferError. Done may only be reported once cargo nextest run -p transfer has run. Resume progress should show up on the status socket, /run/kestrel/status.sock. A migration note for journal format version 2 is still owed.
